title: Toll Plaza Traffic

stimulus.content: A toll plaza monitors the number of cars entering during the morning rush. The rate at which cars enter the plaza, in cars per minute, is modeled by the differentiable function R(t) = 6 + 5 cos(0.16t), where t is measured in minutes after 7:00 AM and 0 \le t \le 30.

prompt: The rate at which cars enter a toll plaza during the morning rush is modeled by R(t) = 6 + 5 cos(0.16t) cars per minute, where t is measured in minutes after 7:00 AM and 0 \le t \le 30.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write, but do not evaluate, a definite integral expression that gives the total number of cars that enter the plaza during the 30 minutes from 7:00 AM to 7:30 AM.

rubricPoints.criterion: Sets up the definite integral with correct limits of integration (0 and 30) and the correct integrand R(t).
commonErrors: uses limits 0 to 15 or 15 to 30 instead of 0 to 30
uses the derivative R'(t) as the integrand
writes an indefinite integral with no limits
forgets the dt
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Writes \int R(t)\,dt with no limits of integration

rubricPoints.criterion: Includes the differential dt and uses correct integral notation in the expression.
commonErrors: missing dt
writes a sum instead of an integral

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the average value of the rate R(t) on the interval 0 \le t \le 30.

rubricPoints.criterion: Sets up the average value formula (1/(30 - 0))\int_0^{30} R(t)\,dt with the correct factor in front.
commonErrors: forgets the 1/30 factor
uses 30 as the denominator outside the integral instead of 30 - 0
sets up the average of values at endpoints only

rubricPoints.criterion: Evaluates the integral correctly and reports the average value, rounded appropriately.
commonErrors: arithmetic error while evaluating the cosine term
rounds to an unreasonable precision
forgets to divide by 30 after integrating
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Integrates correctly but forgets the factor of 1/30 and reports 169.2

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Find the time t, for 0 \le t \le 30, at which the rate R(t) is greatest. Justify your answer.

rubricPoints.criterion: Finds the candidate times (critical points of R and the interval endpoints) and justifies which one gives the maximum rate.
commonErrors: states the answer with no work or reasoning
checks only the critical point and ignores the endpoints
justifies a maximum using a first derivative test done incorrectly
rubricPoints.exampleEarning: Finds R'(t) = -0.8\sin(0.16t), sets it to zero, compares candidates and shows R is greatest at t = 30

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: A second study computes \int_0^{30} L(t)\,dt = 243, where L(t) is the rate at which cars leave the plaza. Interpret this value in the context of the problem.

rubricPoints.criterion: Interprets the integral as the total accumulation of the rate L(t) over the 30 minutes.
commonErrors: says the integral is a rate
confuses cars leaving with the total number of cars in the plaza
describes an average instead of a total
rubricPoints.exampleEarning: Says 243 is the total number of cars that left the plaza over the 30 minutes
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Says 243 cars per minute left the plaza

rubricPoints.criterion: Reports the result with correct units (cars) in context.
commonErrors: no units given
wrong units such as cars per minute
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Gives the number 243 with no units

sampleResponse: (a) The total number of cars entering over the 30 minutes is given by \int_0^{30} R(t)\,dt. (b) The average value is \frac{1}{30}\int_0^{30} R(t)\,dt \approx 5.640 cars per minute. (c) Setting R'(t) = -0.8\sin(0.16t) = 0 gives t = 0 (and no others in the interval); checking the candidates t = 0 and t = 30 shows R(0) = 11 and R(30) \approx 5.29, so the maximum occurs at t = 0. (d) The value 243 represents the total number of cars that left the plaza during the 30 minutes.

title: Particle Along the x-axis

stimulus.content: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 for t \ge 0. At time t = 0, the particle is at position x = 5.

prompt: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its velocity at time t is v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 for t \ge 0. At time t = 0, the particle is located at x = 5.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find all times t, 0 \le t \le 4, at which the particle is at rest.

rubricPoints.criterion: Solves v(t) = 0 correctly and identifies all times in the interval where the velocity is zero.
commonErrors: solves the quadratic incorrectly
reports only one root when there are two
gives times outside the interval 0 to 4
rubricPoints.exampleEarning: Sets 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 0, factors to 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0, and reports t = 1 and t = 3

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particle at time t = 1 and state whether the particle is speeding up or slowing down at that instant.

rubricPoints.criterion: Computes the acceleration a(t) = v'(t) correctly and evaluates a(1), then compares signs of v(1) and a(1) to conclude speeding up or slowing down.
commonErrors: differentiates incorrectly
sign error in a(1)
concludes speeding up without comparing the signs of velocity and acceleration
rubricPoints.exampleEarning: a(t) = 6t - 12, so a(1) = -6 and v(1) = 0; since v(1) = 0 the particle changes direction, and it is speeding up
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Computes a(1) = -6 and calls it slowing down with no discussion of v(1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Find the total distance traveled by the particle from t = 0 to t = 4.

rubricPoints.criterion: Sets up the total distance as \int_0^4 |v(t)|\,dt or splits the interval so the absolute value is handled correctly.
commonErrors: integrates v(t) instead of |v(t)|
integrates |v(t)| with no sign handling and gets the wrong setup
uses the area under v(t) net change instead of total distance
rubricPoints.exampleFailing: Writes \int_0^4 v(t)\,dt and calls it total distance

rubricPoints.criterion: Evaluates the distance integral correctly, accounting for the sign change in v(t).
commonErrors: arithmetic error when evaluating from 0 to 1, 1 to 3, and 3 to 4
forgets that the segment from 1 to 3 is negative and needs flipping
reports the net displacement instead
rubricPoints.exampleEarning: Evaluates to a total distance of 28.5 units

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Find the position of the particle at time t = 3.

rubricPoints.criterion: Uses x(t) = x(0) + \int_0^t v(s)\,ds and evaluates x(3) correctly.
commonErrors: writes x(t) = 5 + v(t) instead of using the integral
evaluates the antiderivative at the wrong endpoint
arithmetic error in the final position

sampleResponse: (a) The particle is at rest when v(t) = 0, so 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0, giving t = 1 and t = 3. (b) a(t) = 6t - 12, so a(1) = -6; since v(1) = 0, the particle is at rest at t = 1 and momentarily changes direction. (c) Total distance is \int_0^4 |v(t)|\,dt = \int_0^1 v(t)\,dt - \int_1^3 v(t)\,dt + \int_3^4 v(t)\,dt, which evaluates to 20 - 8 + 16.5 = 28.5. (d) x(t) = 5 + \int_0^t v(s)\,ds = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 5, so x(3) = 27 - 54 + 27 + 5 = 5.
